To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The unsteady shock – separation interaction is a two-fold mechanism, on the one side being the origin of the self-induced oscillation, on the other side damping the fluctuation of the flow field.

the unsteadiness of the shock-boundary layer interaction is caused by a dynamic coupling between the shock wave motion and a separation bubble, and that the shock-boundary interaction is a two-fold phenomenon, on the one side causing unsteadiness, on the other side damping the unsteadiness.

the unsteady shock wave boundary layer interaction can be divided into two distinct flow regimes: (1) a regime with incipient separation, where the shock wave oscillates in response to the boundary layer fluctuations, and (2) a regime with full-scale separation, where the separation bubble is the origin of the unsteadiness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of the unsteady aerodynamic forces acting on aeroelastic wing structures in the presence of shock-induced separation.
the understanding of the shock-boundary layer interaction in terms of the unsteady pressure distribution and the flow field structure.
aeroelastic effects of the unsteady interaction of shock wave and turbulent separation on the wing structure and on the flow field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the shock wave boundary layer interaction is not the origin of the aerodynamic unsteadyness, but the unsteady shock wave boundary layer separation is the origin of the shock wave boundary-layer interaction.
the unsteady flow is caused by the interaction of shock and turbulent separation, which in turn is caused by the unsteady shock wave motion.
the unsteady flow field over the aeroelastic wing is governed by the shock wave oscillations, which are the origin of the aerodynamic unsteadyness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TR-PIV has proven its capability to provide a time-resolved visualization of unsteady flow fields.
aeroelastic unsteadiness is not necessarily a result of flow separation.
the unsteady interaction of shock wave and turbulent separation is the key feature for the self-induced oscillation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TR-PIV technique is a powerful tool for the analysis of unsteady flow phenomena.
the shock wave oscillations are the result of the unsteady separation of the turbulent boundary layer.
a time resolved visualization of the flow is essential to understand the origin and the nature of unsteady flow over aeroelastic wings.
